<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Appendix</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Datasets</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The experiments were conducted on the following four benchmark datasets:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">HotpotQA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2018)</a></cite> is a large-scale multi-hop QA dataset with 113k question–answer pairs from Wikipedia. Each question requires reasoning over multiple documents, with sentence-level supporting facts provided. It includes diverse queries and comparison questions that test compositional reasoning and explainability, making it a strong benchmark for multi-hop retrieval systems.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2WikiMultiHopQA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al. (2020)</a></cite> is a multi-hop QA dataset combining Wikipedia text with Wikidata triples to evaluate step-by-step reasoning. Each question includes an explicit reasoning path linking entities across documents. The dataset tests compositional reasoning and requires models to use both unstructured text and structured knowledge to answer questions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MusiQue</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Trivedi et al. (2022)</a></cite> is a multi-hop QA benchmark designed to prevent reasoning shortcuts by requiring genuine multi-step reasoning. It includes around 25k questions composed from connected single-hop queries, each requiring 2 to 4 reasoning steps. The dataset emphasizes strong logical dependencies between steps and includes unanswerable variants to test robustness. MuSiQue is more challenging than earlier datasets and highlights significant performance gaps between humans and models.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MultiHopRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang and Yang (2024)</a></cite> is a recent benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation on complex multi-hop queries. Unlike the above QA datasets, MultiHopRAG is specifically built to evaluate end-to-end RAG systems. It includes 2,556 questions over a corpus of English news articles, with answers supported by evidence from 2 to 4 documents. The queries involve temporal and entity-based reasoning and require retrieving and synthesizing information across multiple sources. This makes the dataset well-suited for evaluating our set-wise passage selection approach.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Baselines</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following reranking models are considered as baselines:</p>
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bge-reranker-large</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al. (2023)</a></cite> is a lightweight cross-encoder model from BAAI that scores query–passage pairs using full cross-attention, enabling more accurate relevance judgments than embedding-based models. Fine-tuned on large-scale data, it is commonly used to rescore top-<math id="A1.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> results in retrieval pipelines.
As a strong open-source baseline, it reflects state-of-the-art conventional reranking focused on individual passage relevance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RankLlama</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ma et al. (2024)</a></cite> is a pointwise reranker based on LLaMA-2 7B model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al. (2023)</a></cite>.
Given a query and a candidate passage, it outputs a score to reorder retrieved documents by their relevance.
It demonstrates strong performance in both in-domain and zero-shot settings, serving as a competitive open-source baselines for passage reranking.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RankVicuna</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pradeep et al. (2023a)</a></cite> is a 7B open-source listwise reranker built on the Vicuna 7B model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al. (2023)</a></cite>.
It takes a query and a list of passages as input and outputs a ranked list of passage indices.
Trained with GPT generated supervision, it achieves performance comparable to GPT-3.5 on benchmarks like TREC DL  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Craswell et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Craswell et al. (2021)</a></cite>, providing a transparent alternative to proprietary rerankers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RankZephyr</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pradeep et al. (2023b)</a></cite> is a zero-shot listwise reranker built on the Zephyr-7B model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tunstall et al. (2023)</a></cite>.
Fine-tuned using GPT-4 generated ranking, it outputs ordered lists of passage indices given a query and candidate passages.
It achieves performance close to GPT-4 and even surpassing it on some benchmarks.
Its open-source nature and reproducibility make it a robust baseline for evaluating listwise reranking methods.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FirstMistral</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2024)</a></cite> is a zero-shot listwise reranker based on Mistral 7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al. (2023)</a></cite>. It reframes reranking as a single-token decoding task, enabling fast and efficient passage selection. Despite its simplicity, it achieves competitive performance and serves as a strong open-source baseline to assess the raw ranking ability of modern instruction-tuned LLMs.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RankGPT4</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al. (2024)</a></cite> is a GPT-4-based reranker accessed via OpenAI’s API, used in a zero-shot setting to rank passages given a query. It delivers state-of-the-art performance but is closed-source, non-reproducible, and costly. RankGPT4 serves as an upper-bound baseline to evaluate how well our approach performs against the strongest proprietary reranker.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Additional Experimental Details</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training</span>.
All <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span> variants are fine-tuned using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the base model.
Training is conducted for 5 epochs using AdamW optimizer with a learning rate of <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> and an effective batch size of 512.
We use 16<math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>A100 GPUs and utilize Axolotl<span id="footnote7" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">7</span>
              
              
              
            <a href="https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl</a></span></span></span> framework, which integrates various efficiency-oriented training techniques.
Each model is trained on 40k GPT-4o generated examples, where each input prompt includes a query and 20 retrieved passages.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation Metrics</span>. We evaluate model performance using both retrieval and QA metrics.
For retrieval, we report Mean Receprocal Rank (MRR), Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), Precision, and Recall, which collectively measure the quality of passage ranking and coverage of relevant information.
For end-to-end QA, we adopt Exact Match (EM), F1 score, and Accuracy to quantify answer correctness and completeness.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Additionally, we evaluate <span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">information coverage</span> (<math id="A1.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textit{IC}@k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">IC</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textit{IC}@k</annotation></semantics></math>) on MultiHopRAG benchmark as it provides gold evidence lists, extractively collected from documents.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A1.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\textit{IC}@k=\frac{|\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}\{e|e\in p_{i}\}\cap\{e|e\in\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}\}|}{|\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">IC</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mtext>gold</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mtext>gold</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\textit{IC}@k=\frac{|\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}\{e|e\in p_{i}\}\cap\{e|e\in\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}\}|}{|\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A1.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th top-ranked passage, <math id="A1.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> is an evidence span, <math id="A1.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mtext>gold</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the complete set of annotated gold evidences.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For each question, we collect the complete set of gold evidence <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mtext>gold</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{\text{gold}}</annotation></semantics></math> required to answer it, as annotated in the MultiHopRAG dataset. Given a top-<math id="A1.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> set of retrieved passages, we identify gold evidence spans <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> within the passage text using regular expression matching and remove duplicated evidences if redundant passage exist.
<math id="A1.SS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textit{IC}@k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">IC</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textit{IC}@k</annotation></semantics></math> is then computed as the proportion of gold evidence that appears within the top-<math id="A1.SS3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> passages.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Generation</span>.
For answer generation, we utilize Rankify <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Abdallah et al. (2025)</a></cite> toolkit to implement the full RAG pipeline, which consists of three components: Retrieval, Reranking/Selection, and Generation.
For retrieval, we use the bge-large-en-v1.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al. (2023)</a></cite> model to retrieve the top-20 passages per query.
These candidates are then reranked or filtered via a set-wise selection mechanism.
For generation, we employ Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to generate final answers on general multi-hop QA benchmarks, including HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MusiQUE.
For MultiHopRAG benchmark, we follow the evaluation protocol of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang and Yang (2024)</a></cite> and employ <span id="A1.SS3.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-2024-08-06</span> as the generator due to its strong reasoning performance.
Notably, even when provided with gold evidences, open-source models such as Llama2-70B and Mixtral-8x7B achieve relatively low accuracy (0.32 and 0.36, respectively), while GPT-4 attains a significantly higher score of 0.89, highlighting a substantial performance gap.
The prompts used for each benchmark are shown in Figure <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ A.3 Additional Experimental Details ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Shifting from Ranking to Set Selection for Retrieval Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and Figure <a href="#A1.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ A.3 Additional Experimental Details ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Shifting from Ranking to Set Selection for Retrieval Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, respectively.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F4" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.F4.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="109.89" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 109.89" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,109.89) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 103.99 C 0 107.25 2.64 109.89 5.91 109.89 L 647.24 109.89 C 650.51 109.89 653.15 107.25 653.15 103.99 L 653.15 5.91 C 653.15 2.64 650.51 0 647.24 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2F2;" fill="#F2F2F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 85.78 L 651.18 85.78 L 651.18 5.91 C 651.18 3.73 649.42 1.97 647.24 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 94.38)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.07em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="609.8"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F4.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:44.07em;">
<span id="A1.F4.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F4.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Prompt for General Multi-hop QA</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 13.78)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:41.97em;--ltx-fo-height:4.35em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="60.19" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 60.19)" width="580.75"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F4.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:41.97em;">
<span id="A1.F4.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F4.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{context}

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">Based on these texts, answer these questions:

<br class="ltx_break">Q: {question}

<br class="ltx_break">A:
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Prompt template used for general multi-hop QA datasets including HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MusiQue.</figcaption>
</figure>

<span id="A1.F5.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:41.97em;">
<span id="A1.F5.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F5.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Below is a question followed by some context from different sources. Please answer the question based on the context. The answer to the question is a word or entity. If the provided information is insufficient to answer the question, respond ‘Insufficient Information’. Answer directly without explanation.

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">Question: {question}

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">Context:

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">{context}
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Prompt template used for MultiHopRAG.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Prompt Templates</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide the prompt template used in our experiment for both <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-CoT and <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-Selection only.
Each prompt consists of a question and a set of passages, where each passage is assigned a unique numerical identifier.
In <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-CoT, the prompt concludes with a CoT reasoning, “Let’s think step by step.”, to encourage intermediate reasoning before producing the final selection.
In contrast, <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-Selection only removes this reasoning step and directly instructs the model to output only the final selection without any explanation.
Figure <a href="#A1.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ A.4 Prompt Templates ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Shifting from Ranking to Set Selection for Retrieval Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A1.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ A.4 Prompt Templates ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Shifting from Ranking to Set Selection for Retrieval Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> illustrate the two prompts, respectively.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F6" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.F6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="209.9" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 653.15 209.9" width="653.15"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,209.9) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 204 C 0 207.26 2.64 209.9 5.91 209.9 L 647.24 209.9 C 650.51 209.9 653.15 207.26 653.15 204 L 653.15 5.91 C 653.15 2.64 650.51 0 647.24 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2F2;" fill="#F2F2F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 171.88 L 651.18 171.88 L 651.18 5.91 C 651.18 3.73 649.42 1.97 647.24 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 177.78)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.07em;--ltx-fo-height:1.89em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="26.21" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 26.21)" width="609.8"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:44.07em;">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Prompt for <span id="A1.F6.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-CoT</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.85)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:41.97em;--ltx-fo-height:10.35em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.22em;font-size:10pt;" height="146.29" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 143.21)" width="580.75"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:41.97em;">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">I will provide you with {num} passages, each indicated by a numerical identifier []. Select the passages based on their relevance to the search query: {question}.
<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">{context}

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">Search Query: {question}

<br class="ltx_break">
<br class="ltx_break">Select the passages that mostly cover clear and diverse information to answer the query. Number of passages is unlimited.

<br class="ltx_break">The format of final output should be ‘### Final Selection: [] []’, e.g., ### Final Selection: [2] [1].
<br class="ltx_break">Let’s think step by step.
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>The set-wise passage selection prompt with basic Chain-of-Thought for <span id="A1.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SetR</span>-CoT.</figcaption>
</figure>
